purpose: Teach: インフラ/漁港/眠れる/疲労/行列/砂漠/丘/霧

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、本気で、絶対、町の、絶対、インフラ、絶対、まだ、絶対、整っていなかったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, the town's infrastructure really wasn't built up yet, remember? I think about that sometimes.
lines.style: Settle into the memory slowly. Soft, measured rhythm. Gentle curiosity in the question, not demanding an answer. Let the final thought drift a little.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、本気で、絶対、漁港、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、よく、絶対、見に行ったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Mm, yes. We'd walk out to the fishing port so often back then, didn't we? You remember, don't you, dear?
lines.style: Warm recognition, like she's been waiting for him to bring this up. Voice steady and close. Affectionate on 'dear'—not saccharine, just familiar. Slight nod in her tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、深く、絶対、眠れる、絶対、夜、絶対、ありがたかったぞ、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Your father could sleep so deeply back then. Those quiet nights were a gift, I think. Do you remember, dear?
lines.style: Quieter now, more reflective. The gratitude sits underneath the words—not explained, just felt. Pause slightly before the question. Let it hang a moment.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、疲労、絶対、隠して、絶対、頑張ってきたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Your grandfather hid how tired he was and just kept pushing through. You saw that, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Steadier now, a hint of quiet admiration. Not a complaint—an observation that carries weight. Slight warmth on 'dear.' The realization in her voice that he carried so much.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、町に、絶対、行列、絶対、ができる、絶対、お店、絶対、なかったぞ、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Back then there weren't shops in town where lines would even form. Can you picture that now, Gran?
lines.style: Wondering tone, like he's checking if the contrast is as stark to her as it is to him. Slow enough to let that image land. Slight lift at the question—genuine curiosity.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、テレビで、絶対、砂漠、絶対、初めて、絶対、見たわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: I remember the first time we saw a desert on television. That's how I learned what one looked like, you know?
lines.style: Small smile in the voice. Almost marveling at how limited their world was, without any bitterness. Tender. The discovery was a real thing back then.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、丘、絶対、を、絶対、毎日、絶対、歩いて、絶対、お仕事行ったぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: Your father would walk over that hill every single day to get to work. Every day. Do you remember how much that was, Gran?
lines.style: Slow, deliberate rhythm on the repeated 'every day.' Not mournful—respectful. The physical weight of the routine sits in the voice. Quiet awe at the endurance.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、朝の、絶対、霧、絶対、お祖父ちゃんと、絶対、よく、絶対、見たわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: We'd see the morning mist together so often. Your grandfather and I. Those quiet moments with him—I still see them so clearly.
lines.style: Very soft, almost to herself at first, then drawing you in. The mist is right there. Tender and completely present. The love is in the small details she remembers.
